purpose: Compare fixed nominal means with feedback using identical standardized draws; saved data only
interpretation: Tiny direct command noise alone prevents reproducing the deterministic9-control full turn in each of these five prescribed examples: all fixed-mean branches remain partial at9, without external support/drop.

The paired first actions and full post-first-control states are identical. From control2 onward only the feedback branch recomputes its mean on the changed observation, and its action changes become much larger.
Feedback amplification therefore contributes materially to these recorded divergent commands and failures, while direct physical sensitivity remains when that neural feedback is removed.

These five prescribed examples are not a robustness estimate or a learned-policy success claim. Feedback seed17023 terminates at10; within the matched9-control horizon it remains nonterminal and palm-free. No fixed-mean sequence was extended.
